problem: Most VLN agents simply select among navigable candidates and do not exploit the human ability to anticipate what the next view looks like. Pathdreamer generates future scenes, but substituting them for real observations did not improve VLN performance.
motivation: Humans use common-sense expectations of upcoming scenes (e.g., a hallway with doors, a kitchen with an island) to pick actions. Predicting the semantics of future views could inject such knowledge into agents and help especially on long paths. Patch-level masked image modeling is too costly for VLN, since it multiplies the history length by the number of patches and requires tuning the visual backbone.
key_idea: Pre-train and fine-tune a VLN agent to generate the dVAE visual-token semantics of masked or next views, using efficient overall-image semantic targets and codebook selection, so the agent learns to imagine future views.
insight: Predicting the semantics of future and missing views is a useful auxiliary signal, but only when the targets are made learnable: dynamic codebook selection lets the agent learn from the 8192-token dVAE vocabulary (e.g., APIG SR 64.4 vs 66.3), and weighted or block-weighted patch targets beat mean-patch targets (SR 65.5 vs 68.1). The gain grows with path length (SR +4.2 at length 6 vs 0 at length 3), suggesting imagination helps with long-horizon reasoning. The APIG auxiliary loss in fine-tuning adds only a little (+0.2 to +1.0 SR).
method: Overall image semantics targets: full views are masked and the agent predicts a single distribution over dVAE visual tokens (dVAE from DALL-E, 8192 vocab, 224px, 16px patches). This uses pre-extracted features, keeps the sequence length at A rather than A*N, and skips backbone tuning.

Patch semantic calculation: three target types (mean patch probability, sampled patch conditioned on position embedding, and randomly weighted patch probability conditioned on the sampled weights via FC layers). The weighted type comes with a proof that random weights force per-patch agreement, and a block-wise variant gives higher weights to a random block of B patches.

Codebook selection: static selection keeps the top-|S|=1000 most frequent tokens. Dynamic selection updates a score s_t = λ s_{t-1} + (1-λ)(s_f + γ s_d) from frequency and prediction difficulty, with λ=0.5 and γ=1.

Masked Trajectory Modeling (MTM): 50% of the steps in the trajectory are masked and their view semantics are predicted from the instruction and remaining steps, with an MLP head on the step output and a KL loss.
Masked Panorama Modeling (MPM): 30% of the 36 panorama views are masked and predicted from the instruction, history and surrounding views.

Action Prediction with Image Generation (APIG): predicts next-step view semantics from the instruction [CLS] output (which carries history-conditioned state). It is also used as an auxiliary loss (weight 1) in fine-tuning alongside IL+RL, using mean-patch targets.
Base agents: HAMT is pre-trained from scratch with its 6 tasks plus the 3 new ones. DUET (graph-based) is pre-trained with MPM+APIG only.

setting.backbone: HAMT (history-aware transformer, trained from scratch with added proxy tasks); DUET for the graph-based variant; CLIP-ViT/16 features for HAMT, ViT (ImageNet) features for DUET
setting.model_size: 191M parameters updated in pre-training (vs 260M for the HAMT full model)
setting.training_data: R2R and CVDN training sets (with the HAMT pre-training data/augmentation); dVAE from DALL-E as a pretrained tokenizer; no extra data
setting.observation: 36-view discretized panorama (pre-extracted CLIP-ViT/16 or ViT features) plus navigation history
setting.action_space: discrete navigable viewpoints in the Matterport3D nav-graph

results: On the R2R test leaderboard the DUET-based variant reaches SR 72 / SPL 60, beating DUET (69 / 59). The HAMT-based model gets R2R val-unseen SR 68 / SPL 62 (HAMT 66 / 61), matches HAMT on R2R test (65 / 60), and improves CVDN test GP to 5.83 from 5.58. On R4R and RxR val-unseen it improves over HAMT (RxR SR 60.0 vs 56.5), and its gains are largest on longer paths.
limitations: Gains are small on the R2R test set for the HAMT-based model (65/60, same as HAMT), and the DUET gain with CLIP features on val-unseen SR is negative (72.2 vs 72.8).
Generated semantics are weak: images cannot be reconstructed without at least 70% of the ground-truth tokens, and the auxiliary loss adds only a small gain.
Evaluated only on discrete nav-graph benchmarks in the Matterport3D simulator, with no continuous-environment or real-robot tests.
